claims.affine_family_closure: every generated state at n=17..119 is accepted, with no interior violations; this is finite generator evidence, not an arbitrary-width induction
claims.equality_language_coverage: unproved; only n=5 and n=8 are complete equality corridors, while n=11 and n=14 are fixed traces
claims.exact_codec_and_carrier_round_trip: proved by validation for every accepted input and exercised on every listed state

definitions.acceptance: the canonical atom word has no non-dominant occurrence outside the permitted boundary positions
definitions.atom: previous three-bit packet word, independently OUT-rooted three-face restriction, and local component single/open/carry/close plus carry-in/carry-out flags
definitions.boundary_exceptions: non-dominant atoms are permitted only at the first two and final four packet indices
definitions.compact_global_channel: under the one-carrier rule, left-face mode and packet open/carry/close roles reconstruct global labels without storing CarrierRecord
definitions.constant_bound: at most six exception positions, independent of width
definitions.dominant: maximum atom multiplicity with lexicographically least deterministic tie break
definitions.global_channel: a separate canonical lossless CarrierRecord retains global component labels, exact face slots, and checked cut carriers

limitations: Outside the checked one-carrier discipline, the bounded atom word requires the separate carrier record (or equivalent global labels) for exact frontier expansion.
The affine census stops at n=119; its zero interior violations do not prove arbitrary-width closure.
Complete equality-language coverage is not claimed beyond the enumerated n=5 and n=8 corridors.
Adjacent-width row closure is an endpoint census of fixed generated traces, not a language-level transition induction.

row_transition_closure.definition: for each generated adjacent-width pair, every fixed affine row edge has both endpoint packet words accepted
